sections.question: How much adjusted cash flow from operations before working capital did Eni need in the second half of 2026 to meet the full-year guidance for that measure that it had in place at the end of June 2026? Answer in billions of euros to two decimal places.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Doc 1 (Eni's results for the second quarter and first half of 2026, dated July 29, 2026): "Adjusted net cash before changes in working capital at replacement cost was €7,347 mln in IH ’26", which the same release rounds to "the adjusted operating cash flow (€7.35 bln)".

Step 2. Doc 1's outlook ("Eni is raising guidance for business performance and cash flow generation"; "adjusted CFFO is expected to amount to €15 bln") was published on July 29, 2026, after the end of June, so it was not the guidance in place at the end of June.

Step 3. Doc 2 (Eni's results for the first quarter of 2026, dated April 24, 2026) holds the guidance in place from April 24 until that July update: "adjusted CFFO to amount to €13.8 bln". Doc 2 uses the same measure for actual results: "1Q ’26 Group’s adjusted CFFO before working capital movements was €2.88 bln".

Step 4. Doc 2 and Doc 1: 13.8 - 7.35 = 6.45 (€ billion, two decimal places). Using the exact €7,347 mln instead of the rounded €7.35 bln leaves the two-decimal result unchanged.

Decoy. Doc 1's own outlook, issued on July 29, 2026: 15 - 7.35 = 7.65; it was not yet in place at the end of June.
